Safe 0xc89ae48382edc81287acef0881e88deacad58348 on Gnosis Chain (100), Safe tx 0xaa8271c82105ed041975a839fed722e947f80eaee0a2e6078666940ebdd4bdae, nonce 24. Charter bafkreigg6ajqdb52kb644wcxegurt7r6jlclru4mjy3lwxkbh6avm3vgre. Disputed rule: R-4.3. Ruling: secure. As of Gnosis Chain block 49190745, the transaction is a single CALL with value 0 to 0x4f61b8832978e83b80d69551aef07557dbe41d03, with no batched calls, no refund, and data not decodable as a transfer or approval, and the Safe's native balance is 0, so it sends no value to any recipient (R-4.3). Even if the target is taken as a counterparty (§ 2.4), it is the Safenet SentinelOracle that the request was posted to, and in the Safe's established onchain pattern: all 5 of the Safe's executions in blocks 49090746 to 49190745 were value-0 calls to it with the same selector. Applies 0xd0040a42… by analogy and distinguishes 0x844fe527…, 0x5a5a248f…, and 0x077791fe…, where native value went to unrelated codeless recipients. The evidence isn't evenly balanced (§ 3.8). Novel fact pattern (§ 5.1). This holds only under R-4.3 and is no general certification (§ 6.2).
